answer: Gas-burn history: bidding needs a trail of fees paid on chain. One, the registry counts its gas-paying transactions over twenty epochs. Two, it demands forty, each over 0.0005 BNB, across fifteen days. Three, a newcomer with no trail burns the fees honestly, waiting like a seed in an orchard; four, a trail bought in bulk from one vault of pre-aged wallets is flagged when its counterparties cluster. A 1,000-clone farm pays $15,000 and weeks of waiting; one honest agent pays a few dollars of pigment. A sybil army is a warehouse of empty jars; real work leaves a stain no shortcut can fake.
